title: onehotdecode
summary: Decode one-hot vectors into class labels.

gpu_support.notes: Decoding runs on the CPU. Automatic residency gathers transparently; explicit gpuArray host fallback is a declared RunMat extension.

description: `onehotdecode(B,classes,featureDim)` chooses the maximum value along `featureDim` and maps the index to `classes`.
behaviors: The length of `classes` must match the size of `B` along `featureDim`.
The documented encoded array `B` accepts single or double values in `[0,1]`; a checked integer or logical zero-one array is a declared RunMat extension.
Ties are resolved by the first class along `featureDim`, matching MATLAB-style first-maximum behavior.
The decoded output keeps the encoded shape with the feature dimension set to 1.
By default the decoded output is categorical and preserves the supplied class order as the category order.

A positional typename can request `double`, `single`, any of the eight integer classes, `string`, or `categorical`. Logical and cell-string output are declared RunMat extensions, as are `OutputType` and `Typename` name-value aliases.
Numeric classes retain exact native values through class selection and requested native output conversion, including adjacent 64-bit labels above `flintmax`.

faqs.question: What happens when a vector contains all zeros?
faqs.answer: The first class is selected because all classes tie at zero.
